readings.title: The Test of the False Prophet
readings.subtitle: Guarding the Unbroken Connection of Emunah
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 13:1] “When there arises among you a prophet or a dreamer of dreams, and he shall give you a sign or a wonder,
[2] and the sign or the wonder shall come true, of which he has spoken to you, saying, ‘Let us go after other mighty ones – which you have not known – and serve them,’
[3] do not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is trying you to know whether you love <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> with all your heart and with all your being.
[4] “Walk after <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> and fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>Him</dn>, and guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> commands and obey <dn>His</dn> voice, and serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>Him</dn> and cling to <dn>Him</dn>.
[5] “And that prophet or that dreamer of dreams is put to death, because he has spoken apostasy against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> – who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim and ransomed you from the house of bondage – to make you stray from the way in which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded you to walk. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst.
[6] “When your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom, or your friend who is as your own being, entices you secretly, saying, ‘Let us go and serve other mighty ones’– which you have not known, neither you nor your fathers,
[7] of the mighty ones of the people which are all around you, near to you or far off from you, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth –
[8] do not agree with him or listen to him, nor shall your eye pardon him, nor spare him or conceal him,
[9] but you shall certainly kill him. Your hand is first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hand of all the people,
[10] and you shall stone him with stones until he dies, because he sought to entice you away from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, from the house of bondage.
[11] “And let all Yisra’ěl hear and fear, and not again do any such evil matter as this in your midst.
[12] “When you hear someone in one of your cities, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> gives you to dwell in, saying,
[13] Some men, sons of Beliya‛al, have gone out of your midst and led <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of their city astray, saying, “Let us go and serve other mighty ones” ’ – mighty ones whom you have not known –
[14] then you shall inquire, search out, and ask diligently. And see if the matter is true and established that this abomination was done in your midst,
[15] you shall certainly strike <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, putting <dn>את</dn> it under the ban, and <dn>את</dn> all that is in it and <dn>את</dn> its livestock, with the edge of the sword.
[16] “And gather <dn>את</dn> all its plunder into the middle of the street, and completely burn with fire <dn>את</dn> the city and <dn>את</dn> all its plunder, before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. And it shall be a heap forever, never to be built again.
[17] “And none of that which is put under the ban is to cling to your hand, so that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> turns from the fierceness of <dn>His</dn> displeasure and shall show you compassion, love you and increase you, as <dn>He</dn> swore to your fathers,
[18] when you obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to guard <dn>את</dn> all <dn>His</dn> commands which I command you today, to do what is right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: The Dietary Instructions
readings.subtitle: Distinguishing the Clean from the Unclean
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 14:1] “You are the children of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. Do not cut yourselves nor shave the front of your head for the dead,
[2] for you are a set-apart people to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has chosen you to be a people for <dn>Himself</dn>, a treasured possession above all the peoples who are on the face of the earth.
[3] “Do not eat whatever is abominable.
[4] “These are the living creatures which you do eat: ox, sheep, and goat,
[5] deer, and gazelle, and roebuck, and wild goat, and mountain goat, and antelope, and mountain sheep.
[6] “And every beast that has a split hoof divided in two, chewing the cud, among the beasts, you do eat.
[7] “But of those chewing the cud or those having a split hoof completely divided, you do not eat, <dn>את</dn> such as these: <dn>את</dn> the camel, and <dn>את</dn> the hare, and <dn>את</dn> the rabbit, for they chew the cud but do not have a split hoof, they are unclean for you.
[8] “And <dn>את</dn> the pig is unclean for you, because it has a split hoof, but does not chew the cud. You do not eat their flesh or touch their dead carcasses.
[9] “These you do eat of all that are in the waters: all that have fins and scales you do eat.
[10] “And whatever does not have fins and scales you do not eat, it is unclean for you.
[11] “Any clean bird you do eat,
[12] but these you do not eat: the eagle, and the vulture, and the black vulture,
[13] and the red kite, and the falcon, and the buzzard after their kinds,
[14] and every raven after its kind,
[15] and the ostrich, and the nighthawk, and the seagull, and the hawk after their kinds,
[16] the little owl, and the great owl, and the white owl,
[17] and the pelican, and the carrion vulture, and the fisher owl,
[18] and the stork, and the heron after its kind, and the hoopoe and the bat.
[19] “And every creeping insect that flies is unclean for you, they are not eaten.
[20] “Any clean bird you do eat.
[21] “Do not eat whatever dies of itself. Give it to the stranger who is within your gates, to eat it, or sell it to a foreigner. For you are a set-apart people to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. Do not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.

readings.title: The Law of the Tithe
readings.subtitle: Rejoicing Before the Creator
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 14:22] “You shall tithe without fail <dn>את</dn> all the yield of your grain that the field brings forth year by year.
[23] “And you shall eat before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, in the place where <dn>He</dn> chooses to make <dn>His</dn> Name dwell, the tithe of your grain and your new wine and your oil, and of the firstlings of your herds and your sheep, so that you learn to fear <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> always.
[24] “But when the way is too long for you, so that you are not able to bring the tithe, or when the place where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses to put <dn>His</dn> Name is too far from you, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is blessing you,
[25] then you shall give it in silver, and shall take the silver in your hand and go to the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses.
[26] “And you shall use the silver for whatever your being desires: for cattle or sheep, for wine or strong drink, for whatever your being desires. And you shall eat there before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and you shall rejoice, you and your household.
[27] “And do not forsake the Lěvite who is within your gates, for he has no part nor inheritance with you.
[28] “At the end of every third year you bring out <dn>את</dn> all the tithe of your increase of that year and store it up within your gates.
[29] “And the Lěvite, because he has no portion nor inheritance with you, and the sojourner and the fatherless and the widow who are within your gates, shall come and eat and be satisfied, so that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> does bless you in all the work of your hand which you do.

readings.title: The Year of Release
readings.subtitle: Canceling Debt and Eradicating Poverty
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 15:1] “At the end of every seven years you make a release of debts.
[2] “And this is the word of the release: Every creditor is to release what he has loaned to his neighbour, he does not require it of <dn>את</dn> his neighbour or <dn>את</dn> his brother, because it is called the release of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[3] “Of <dn>את</dn> a foreigner you could require it, but your hand is to release whatever is owed by your brother.
[4] “Only, there should be no poor among you. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does greatly bless you in the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you to possess as an inheritance,
[5] only if you diligently obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to guard to do <dn>את</dn> all these commands which I am commanding you today.
[6] “For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall bless you as <dn>He</dn> promised you. And you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow. And you shall rule over many nations, but they do not rule over you.
[7] “When there is a poor man with you, one of your brothers, within any of the gates in your land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, do not harden <dn>את</dn> your heart nor shut <dn>את</dn> your hand from your poor brother,
[8] for you shall certainly open your hand to him and certainly lend him enough for his need, whatever he needs.
[9] “Be on guard lest there be a thought of Beliya‛al in your heart, saying, ‘The seventh year, the year of release, is near,’ and your eye is evil against your poor brother and you give him naught. And he shall cry out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> against you, and it shall be a sin in you.
[10] “You shall certainly give to him, and your heart should not be grieved when you give to him, because for this reason <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> does bless you in all your works and in all to which you put your hand.
[11] “Because the poor one does not cease from the land. Therefore I am commanding you, saying, ‘You shall certainly open your hand to your brother, to your poor and to your needy one, in your land.’

readings.title: The Release of the Hebrew Servant
readings.subtitle: Supplying the Freed Slave
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 15:12] “When your brother is sold to you, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, and shall serve you six years, then let him go free from you in the seventh year.
[13] “And when you send him away free from you, let him not go away empty-handed.
[14] “You shall richly supply him from your flock, and from your threshing-floor, and from your winepress. With that which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has blessed you with, give to him.
[15] “And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Mitsrayim, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> ransomed you. Therefore I am commanding you <dn>את</dn> this word today.
[16] “And it shall be, when he says to you, ‘I do not go away from you,’ because he loves you and your house, because it is good for him with you,
[17] then you shall take <dn>את</dn> an awl and thrust it through his ear to the door, and he shall be your servant forever. Do the same to your female servant.
[18] “Let it not be hard in your eyes when you send him away free from you, for he has been worth a double hired servant in serving you six years. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall bless you in all that you do.

readings.title: The Firstborn Males
readings.subtitle: Consecrating the Flock and Herd
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 15:19] “Set apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> all the first-born males that come from your herd and your flock. Do no work with the first-born of your herd, nor shear the first-born of your flock.
[20] “You and your household are to eat it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> year by year in the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chooses.
[21] “But when there is any defect in it, lame or blind, or has any evil defect, do not slaughter it to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[22] “Eat it within your gates – the unclean and the clean alike – as the gazelle, and as the deer.
[23] “Only, do not eat <dn>את</dn> its blood, pour it on the ground like water.

readings.section: Calendar Bias & The Rejection of Babylon
readings.title: The Three Pilgrimage Festivals
readings.subtitle: Holy Rehearsals of the Redemptive Plan
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 16:1] “Guard <dn>את</dn> the new moon of Aḇiḇ, and perform the Pěsaḥ to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, for in the new moon of Aḇiḇ <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> brought you out of Mitsrayim by night.
[2] “And you shall slaughter the Pěsaḥ to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, from the flock and the herd, in the place where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chooses to put <dn>His</dn> Name.
[3] “Eat no leavened bread with it. For seven days you eat unleavened bread with it, bread of affliction, because you came out of the land of Mitsrayim in haste – so that you remember <dn>את</dn> the day in which you came out of the land of Mitsrayim, all the days of your life.
[4] “And no leaven should be seen with you in all your border for seven days, neither should any of the meat which you slaughter in the evening on the first day stay all night until morning.
[5] “You are not allowed to slaughter <dn>את</dn> the Pěsaḥ within any of your gates which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> gives you,
[6] but at the place where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses to make <dn>His</dn> Name dwell, there you slaughter <dn>את</dn> the Pěsaḥ in the evening, at the going down of the sun, at the appointed time you came out of Mitsrayim.
[7] “And you shall roast and eat it in the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses, and in the morning you shall turn and go to your tents.
[8] “Six days you eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there is a closing festival to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> – you do no work.
[9] "Count seven weeks for yourself. Begin to count seven weeks from the time you begin to put the sickle to the grain.
[10] “And you shall perform the Festival of Shaḇuʽoth to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, according to the voluntary offering from your hand, which you give as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> blesses you.
[11] “And you shall rejoice before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, you and your son and your daughter, and your male servant and your female servant, and the Lěvite who is within your gates, and the stranger and the fatherless and the widow who are in your midst, at the place where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses to make <dn>His</dn> Name dwell.
[12] “And you shall remember that you were a slave in Mitsrayim, and you shall guard and do <dn>את</dn> these laws.
[13] “Perform the Festival of Sukkot for seven days after the ingathering from your threshing-floor and from your winepress,
[14] and you shall rejoice in your festival, you and your son and your daughter, and your male servant and your female servant, and the Lěvite, and the stranger and the fatherless and the widow who are within your gates.
[15] “For seven days you shall celebrate to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chooses, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> does bless you in all your increase and in all the work of your hands, and you shall be only rejoicing!
[16] “Three times a year all your males appear before <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in the place which <dn>He</dn> chooses: at the Festival of Matzot, and at the Festival of Shaḇuʽoth, and at the Festival of Sukkot. And none should appear before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> empty-handed,
[17] but each one with the gift of his hand, according to the blessing of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> which <dn>He</dn> has given you.

readings.title: Appointing Judges and Officers
readings.subtitle: Following Righteousness Alone
readings.text:
[Deuteronomy 16:18] “Appoint judges and officers within all your gates, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, according to your tribes. And they shall judge the people with righteous right-ruling.
[19] “Do not distort right-ruling. Do not show partiality, nor take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
[20] “Follow righteousness, righteousness alone, so that you live and inherit the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you.
[21] “Do not plant for yourself any tree as an Ashěrah near the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> that you make for yourself.
[22] “And do not set up a pillar, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> hates.
